Ammonia product chemical potential, recovery and factory costs
ROOT, 12 November 2026 Brisbane. Original conditional engineering calculations from the complete available ammonia return and separately read primary sources. No producer ZIP/code, supplementary artifact or physical experiment was collected or executed. No new catalyst, separator, lifetime or factory is supplied by these calculations.

1. What the worked process actually leaves open
The available candidate combines hot wet hydroxide electrolysis/PdAg hydrogen transfer, a separately dried BaH2-BaO/Fe/CaH2 synthesis loop and MgCl2 capture/release. Its conditional 1kg/day, 245C/18bar result is11.896kWh/kg steady,14.09 with startup allocated over100h production,14.84 including assumed lifecycle preparation, and$3.379/kg at1t/day. A100-hour useful-output interval begins AFTER conditioning; a cold100-hour calendar window is different. These are source-reported calculations, not ROOT-executed producer code or measured plant performance.
The process needs333m2 fabricated membrane,7.07t catalyst,2.41t sorbent and1761m2 recuperator area at1t/day. Those inventories and working states, not an isolated electrode potential, determine the cost.

2. A bookkeeping bound that a cheaper catalyst cannot remove
The displayed cost table sums to$3.379/kg. Waiving ALL capital recovery1.279, maintenance.219 and decommissioning.017 still leaves$1.864/kg with every other stated operation unchanged. Waiving ONLY membrane/catalyst/sorbent replacement leaves$2.531/kg. These are exact deletions within the displayed ledger, NOT physical lower bounds across architectures.
Therefore neither a free factory at otherwise identical performance nor long material life by itself reaches$1/kg. At least the actual recurring process and fabrication/inventory architecture must change together. Doubling an isolated catalyst rate does not give such a change; the producer's own conditional sensitivity still exceeds$3/kg.
The previous independent stoichiometry/purge note shows why delivered-H2 boundary, inert buildup, actual gas recovery and catalyst inventory must also close. A purchased-system energy figure with an unspecified outlet pressure must not be combined with a compressor already inside its boundary.
